Hi Sofia 


Thanks again for your time today. Quick post-call recap and next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary from call:
- You're evaluating Redwood for customer support augmentation (intent classification + response draft).
- Primary concerns: handling of PII in prompts/outputs, data residency, logs/retention, and audit evidence for procurement.
- Target: pilot in Q4 with a potential expansion if controls meet Acme's security bar.

Action items we'll take now:
1) Share written confirmation on how prompts/inputs and outputs are stored and retained for Redwood hosted and Dedicated/Private deployments (see attached: redwood-pii-dataflow.pdf).
2) Provide SOC2 summary + pointer to compliance artifacts during the security call.
3) Schedule a 45m security deep-dive next week with our infra/security engineer.

Quick answers from today (high-level):
- Hosted API (default): request logs (includes prompts and generated outputs and minimal metadata) are retained for 30 days by default and used for abuse detection and service quality improvement. Enterprise customers can opt out of improvement-use or configure retention via contract.
- Redwood Dedicated: logs are stored in your dedicated environment; retention is configurable (we typically advise 90/180/365-day buckets).
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): no Redwood-hosted copies \u2014 data remains in your environment per your retention policy.

I'll follow up with a detailed note from engineering/legal that answers the specific questions you raised on redaction, access controls, and exportability. Please confirm a few times that work for your security team for next week.

Thanks \u2014
Neha Kapoor

Thanks, Neha \u2014 really helpful summary. A few specific clarifications our security/procurement team needs before we proceed: 

1) Prompts/inputs and model outputs: are these stored persistently by default for Hosted API? If so, where (region), for how long, and who has access?
2) Can we opt out of Redwood using our data for model improvement on hosted plan, or is that only for enterprise contracts?
3) Are there built-in redaction options (automatic PII masking) or recommended SDK patterns to prevent sensitive data from being logged?
4) For Dedicated: you mentioned logs are in our environment \u2014 does Redwood ever take backups off-site? Who manages encryption keys?
5) We need SOC2 Type II or equivalent evidence and any audit logs that show access to raw prompts/outputs.

I've attached our security questionnaire (Acme_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx) with the fields our InfoSec requires. Can you provide answers inline or via the security call?

Best,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Trust & Safety | Acme Financial
sofia.martinez@acmefin.com

Hi Sofia \u2014 thanks for the detailed questions. I pulled together the confirmed answers with input from engineering and legal. I'll keep these concise and we can expand on the security call.

Short answers (by deployment):

1) Hosted API (Redwood-managed):
- What is stored: By default, request logs contain the raw prompt (input), model output (generated response), and minimal request metadata (timestamp, model id, truncated session id).
- Where: stored in Redwood's encrypted object stores in the region of the API endpoint (we support us and eu regions; see region selection in the console).
- Retention: default 30 days. Can be adjusted via Enterprise contract; we offer opt-out for \"improvement use\" for Enterprise customers (we can disable using your data for model improvements).
- Access: encrypted at rest; access limited to a small, audited set of infra/service accounts. All access is logged and available in audit exports for Enterprise customers.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- What is stored: logs and metrics are stored in your dedicated instance. By default, we keep 90 days, but retention is configurable.
- Backups/off-site: Redwood does not take customer data backups off-site without explicit agreement. Standard practice is encrypted snapshots stored in a customer-dedicated tenancy; we can arrange customer-managed encryption keys (via KMS/HSM) for stronger key separation.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem):
- What is stored: No Redwood-hosted copies. All prompt/output data stored in your environment only. Retention and backup policies are governed by your IT.

4) PII/redaction options:
- Runtime redaction: we provide SDK client-side redaction helpers (patterns & regex templates) and a managed pre-processing filter library you can deploy in your pipeline to strip or tokenise sensitive fields before sending.
- Server-side masking: for Enterprise, we can apply post-processing redaction hooks and automatic regex-based scrubbing on logs on ingest.

5) Use for improvement & opt-out:
- By default hosted data may be used for abuse detection and service quality. Enterprise contracts include an explicit opt-out clause for model-improvement usage and can add longer retention or immediate deletion requirements.

6) Audit evidence & SOC2:
- We maintain SOC2 Type II; I've attached a high-level SOC2 summary and a redwood-pii-dataflow.pdf that maps where logs live and how they're accessed. Full attestations/certificates and more granular audit logs can be shared under NDA/Procurement.

Next steps I propose: 
- I'll populate your security questionnaire (inline answers) and send back a completed copy before the security call.
- Please share 2-3 time slots for a 45m meeting with your security team next week and we'll include our infra/security engineer and legal SMEs.

If you prefer, we can also set up a Dedicated pilot where we preconfigure retention and disabled improvement-use to match your policy.

Thanks \u2014
Nikhil Sharma
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai
